literal: Even millet-measure not-sulking is needed, even palmyra-measure desire abundantly if comes.
translation: When desire swells as vast as a palmyra tree, one must not sulk even as much as a tiny millet seed.
modern: காமம் பனை மரத்தின் அளவாக நிறைந்து வரும்போது, தினை அளவுகூட ஊடல் கொள்ளாமல் இருக்க வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts two traditional measures of size: the tiny millet seed (தினை) and the massive palmyra tree (பனை). The speaker reflects on the overwhelming nature of her desire for reunion with her lover. When love and desire swell to the immense size of a palmyra tree, there is no room left for feigned anger or lovers' quarrels (ஊடல்). Therefore, she resolves that she must not sulk even a tiny millet's worth, as her vast affection completely overpowers any minor grievances.
